thread.title: Apple Earnings: A Tie-Breaker for the Faangs - Barron's

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Apple Earnings: A Tie-Breaker for the Faangs - Barron's
text:
By Teresa Rivas July 30, 2018 4:04 p.m. ET Tech stocks have led the market to gains in recent years, but recent fumbles put the sector's relentless march higher in question.
Where we were: Tech has soared in recent years, becoming as important to the S&P 500 as it was before the dot-com bubble; seen as an oasis from trade-war worries, it hadn't lost much steam despite recent market volatility.
Where we're headed: Apple (AAPL) reports earnings this week, the last of the Faangs to do so. With two components rising on earnings and two falling (hard); the way it breaks post-results may shed more light on where tech is going.
Illustration: Joel Arbaje, Source Photo: courtesy of Apple Tech's dominance has led the market to new highs in recent years and boosted its weighting in the S&P 500 to its highest level since the dot com bubble .
In recent days, however, that's been a mixed blessing: Facebook (FB) lost $119 billion in market value in one day and Netflix (NFLX) tanked after its earnings , too. The latter is still up 75% year to date, while Facebook is now in the red, both year to date, and in the past 12 months. Both stocks' multiyear runs are still intact.
But at the same time, Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) jumped after its report , and Amazon.com (AMZN) flexed its muscles with a strong quarter as well, putting it in a race with Apple (AAPL) to be the first company to reach a trillion-dollar market capitalization.
Speaking of Apple, it will report this week, making it the last of the Faang stocks to do so. And while its results are always newsworthy, they seem especially important this time around. With the Faangs tied two-to-two for post-earnings declines, Apple could cast the deciding vote, as it were, if the second quarter is another tech triumph or a downfall.
The issue is particularly relevant this time around precisely because the bull market is so long in the tooth and nervous investors may be looking for any excuse to sell. ( Morgan Stanley , for its part, believes we're in for another February-level correction .) Some may see disappointing results from the majority of the Faang stocks as a sign that it's the beginning of the end for tech, and while the S&P 500 could still push higher without drafting behind tech's rise, it will be much harder.
The Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) is trading down again today, off 1.4% this afternoon, with all five Faang stocks in the red.
But U.S. tech companies aren't the only ones getting hit: Their Chinese counterparts are also selling off, hurt by a trio of earnings reports. Sohu.com (SOHU) is down more than 13% after reporting second-quarter earnings . The media firm lost $1.27 per American depositary share on revenue of $486.01 million. Analysts were looking for a loss of $1.50 per ADS on revenue of $506.79 million. For the full year, it sees a loss of $1.40 to $1.65 per ADS, on revenue of $445 million to $470 million. Consensus calls for a loss of 96 cents per ADS on revenue of $556.7 million.
Sogou (SOGO) is off nearly 8% after its second-quarter earnings : The search engine provider earned nine cents per ADS, better than the consensus estimate for seven cents, but Sogou's revenue of $301.4 million was below the average analyst estimate of $304.5 million, and it issued a disappointing forecast for the third quarter.
Likewise, Changyou.com (CYOU) is falling 13.7% after its second quarter . The gaming firm earned 52 cents per ADS on revenue of $112.83 million, while analysts were looking for earnings of 45 cents per ADS on revenue of $118.68 million. It also offered light third-quarter guidance.
The KraneShares CSI china Internet ETF (KWEB) is off 3% to $56.08 this afternoon.
